description:
Age guidance: 14+. Belgrade, 1914. Three hungry young men are offered something to eat (and the chance to change the course of history).  

Their mission: kill Archduke Franz Ferdinand and set the century alight.  

A wild, heartfelt and occasionally accurate tale of history’s most reluctant radicals, from Rajiv Joseph (Guards at the Taj, Bengal Tiger at the Baghdad Zoo). Lyndsey Turner (The Crucible, 1536) directs, designed by Es Devlin.
name: Archduke

description:
Running time: approximately 65mins. Age guidance: 16+. Porn. Deepfakes. Disappearing girls. A journalist wired to a machine. A mother’s grief sold for clicks.

As the lines blur between entertainment and abuse, technology and sex, violence and voyeurism - who’s complicit and who is in control?

Georgie Dettmer makes her professional playwriting debut.
name: Are You Watching?

description: 60-75 minute Backstage Tours (with catering package options)
name: Backstage Tour
attribute_TicketVenue1: Royal Court Theatre, Sloane Square, SW1W 8AS

description:
Age guidance: 14+. (65mins) Yousef was raised as a Christian-Arab-Palestinian-Israeli kid in Haifa, and is now raising two Jewish-Arab-Austrian kids in Berlin. Only he’s facing a custody battle, so things are getting complicated...
A story about family, fear, and imagining a future beyond borders.
name: Between The River and The Sea

description:
Age guidance: 14+. Bullock Creek, South Carolina, 1862: Ginnie Good raises five children in a cabin as a war rages outside.  Today: A woman rents the cabin on AirBnB to conjure her ancestors.  

Joy Nesbitt makes her Royal Court debut with this new play about complicated histories, belonging - and what we hear when we listen to the voices of the past, directed by Tatenda Shamiso.
name: Blood of my Blood

description:
To celebrate our 70th Anniversary year, we’re reading a groundbreaking play from the Royal Court’s history every month – and then hosting a Book Club to chat about the play together.

We will have copies of each month’s script available in our Box Office to drop in and read in advance – just please don’t take the book away with you!
name: Book Club

description:
'Familiar red walls. Voices from within.'

Court in Progress
One night. Seven new pieces. Brought to you by the staff of the Royal Court. 

Join us in the Undercroft Bar for our now bi-annual scratch night, featuring a line up seven 'works in progress' pieces: written, directed and performed by artists working within the theatre. It aims to recognise their artistic credo, provide them with a platform to share and celebrate their work, and facilitate an opportunity for inter-departmental creative exchange within our iconic vermillion walls. 

"Our front line teams at the Royal Court are made up of brilliant writers, directors, actors and creatives making work all across London." - David Byrne, Artistic Director, via The Stage.

Court in Progress was founded by Phoebe Coop in 2024 and continues for its third outing on the Saturday 7th March. 

Supported generously by the Royal Court Theatre.
name: Court in Progress

description: Open to anyone who has already attended or will attend the show (not limited to those with a ticket for the 24th June).
name: Director's Night for Are You Watching?

description: Open to anyone who has already attended or will attend the show (not limited to those with a ticket for the 16th April).
name: Directors' Night for John Proctor is the Villain

description:
Join Jessica Swale – the Olivier Award-winning playwright of Nell Gwynn and Blue Stockings, and writer of current smash-hit Paddington The Musical – to explore the value of using play and exercises in your creative writing practice.

Kickstart your imagination with fun and rewarding tasks drawn from her new book A Year of Creative Thinking: 366 Daily Inspirations for Writers and Artists. This session is an open-hearted invitation to try new things, test your limits and unlock your creative potential. The workshop will end with a Q&A and book signing.
name: Establishing a Daily Creative Practice, with Jessica Swale

description: First Words is a group for writers in the first year of parenthood.  It is not a formal writers' group.  It is also not a creche.  It is a chance for writers with babies under the age of one to meet each other - to build community in what can be an isolating experience, and to be seen not just as parents, but as writers too.  There will be free tea and coffee.  There will be (basic) soft play.  There will - we hope - be other people who have some shared understanding of what this stage of life is like.  There will be no expectation to write a single word. First Words is not about writing - it's about recognising that you are a writer, even if you don't write anything, for months or years. The Royal Court's aim is to be a home for all writers - First Words is a home for writers' babies too.
name: First Words

description:
Since 2001, the Genesis Foundation has nurtured the careers of thousands of exceptionally talented artists and creative professionals.

To celebrate its first 25 years, the Foundation is hosting its anniversary show ​. All proceeds will contribute directly to the success of training, mentoring and development programmes run in partnership with highly respected cultural organisations. 

If you would like to make a further donation, please visit genesisfoundation.org.uk/donate
name: Genesis Foundation 25th Anniversary Show

description:
‘Everything is going to be all right.’  

An expectant couple wait in a hospital room as the future they had planned unravels.   

A story about impossible choices and enduring love.  

Rosie Sheehy and Robert Aramayo star in this world premiere by Luke Norris (Goodbye to All That), directed by Jeremy Herrin (People, Places and Things).
name: Guess How Much I Love You?

description:
Running time: 1 hour and 45 mins (approx) NO INTERVAL
Age guidance: 12 +. Five young women running on pop music, optimism, and fury are about to shed light on the darkest secrets in their small town.  

A story about girlhood, power, and questioning the narratives we’ve been taught. 

Danya Taymor directs Kimberly Belflower’s bitingly funny, seven-time Tony Award-nominated fresh take on Arthur Miller’s The Crucible.
name: John Proctor is the Villain

description:
Running time: approximately 1 hour 20 minutes. Age guidance: 14+. On his 69th birthday, a man sits alone and listens to the echoes of his younger self. 

Krapp’s Last Tape returns to the Royal Court, where it played in 1958, with a new production by York Theatre Royal. 

Opening the performance every night is Godot’s To-Do List, by Leo Simpe-Asante. Winner of the 2025 inaugural Royal Court Young Playwrights Award, this curtain-raising comedy follows seven decades on from Krapp’s Last Tape’s own debut as a curtain-raiser on our stage.
name: Krapp's Last Tape / Godot's To-Do List

description:
A book launch for Leo Butler's new book 'Notes From A Working Class Playwright'. Award-winning British playwright, Leo Butler looks back over 25 years of writing for the stage and his extensive experience teaching and mentoring emerging playwrights through the Royal Court Young Writers' Programme. Join us to celebrate the launch of his new book Notes From A Working Class Playwright. Drinks reception and opportunity to buy a signed copy of the book from 7pm, readings and Q&A from 7:45.
This event is free to join but spaces are limited - you must book a free ticket to be added to the guest list. Please let us know at writerscard@royalcourttheatre.com if you are no longer able to attend.
20 free spaces for WC members
name: Leo Butler Book Launch

description:
Age guidance: 14+. In 1930s Germany, a woman puts on her dead husband’s trousers and never takes them off. 
As the world around her changes, she endures war and dictatorship, hunger and humiliation – always fighting to stay alive.  

More than 30 years after she first brought the role to life, Tilda Swinton makes a long-awaited return to stage as Ella/Max in Manfred Karge’s Man to Man - the role she originated in the acclaimed 1988.
name: Man to Man

description:
With the eyes of the world watching, a Welsh farming community, torn apart by tragedy, gathers to debate a planned memorial.

Age guidance: 14+. Tonight, you’re in the village hall with them – and every vote counts.

A portrait of a close-knit community wrestling with its past, its future and the politics of remembrance.
name: Monument

description:
The founding promise of the Royal Court Theatre since 1956 is simple: anyone in the world writing in English can send us their play, we will read it, and if it's good enough it can make its way to our stages. The plays have been coming ever since, and in 2026 that promise is more vital to the playwriting ecology than ever before.

Got a play you're ready to share with the world? Join key members of the Royal Court's artistic team to discuss our Open Submissions process in glorious detail. Discover how the submissions process works, learn what we're looking for and how you can put your best foot forward as a writer submitting your work to us.

This is a free, ticketed event for Writers' Card members.
name: Open Submissions: How does it work?
Open Technical Session for Guess How Much I Love You?

Open tech rehearsal 1.30pm-6pm.
Attendees gather in the balcony bar at 1:30 for a 30 minute chat with the assistant director. 2-6PM attendees watch JPITV tech from the back of the JTD circle.

description: Maddie Hindes is Commissioning Editor for Plays at Nick Hern Books - the UK’s leading specialist theatre publisher - responsible for reading and acquiring the best contemporary plays for publication and amateur licensing. This talk will offer a step-by-step walkthrough of the process of publishing plays: how publishers discover new writers; explaining contracts and royalties; putting the plays on the page; and how the finished playtexts are shared with the world.
name: Play Publishing: How It Works

name: Supercool test event

name: Teacher's Drop In

description:
Age guidance: 14+. Zambia, 1964: the space race has a new contender. 

As the world’s great powers set their sights on the moon, a schoolteacher gathers a group of misfit dreamers and trains them for lift-off. 

The true(ish) story of the Zambian Space Program, and a nation’s defiant dream to reach for the stars.
name: The Afronauts

description:
Age guidance: 14+. Tens of thousands of years ago, Britain’s earliest inhabitants learn that love and violence feed the same fire. 

When strangers arrive at a secluded cave, domestic harmony shatters – and survival turns savage.
name: The Shitheads

name: What Makes Black Theatre?

description:
Fancy a free coffee and a chat? We’re here for you.

We know avenues for independent and freelance writers seeking guidance can be limited, and the challenges for those developing creative careers can feel overwhelming. So, we’re here to help talk it out with regular, light-touch career surgeries for Writers’ Card Members.

Once a month on a Monday afternoon, we’ll offer up the expertise of the Royal Court’s staff team to discuss anything that’s on your mind. Primarily hosted in our Bar & Kitchen – with tea and coffee on us – we’ll also offer zoom options for those who can’t make it in person.

Topics could include career trajectories, finding opportunities, producing and marketing your own work, accessing funding and support, goat herding, telekinesis, and more - anything where a 20-minute chat might genuinely help or be a useful sounding-board. And from time to time, we’ll offer special sessions dedicated to key areas of expertise.

Slots are available for Members only, in-person at the Royal Court Bar & Kitchen, or via Zoom.

Places are first-come, first-served and the booking portal will open two weeks in advance of each surgery date.
name: Writers' Card: Career Surgeries (in-person)

description:
Come for lunch!

Once a month, we’re offering lunch for a fiver for writers who want to base themselves at the Royal Court for the day, get some work done, and have a chat.

On monthly Fridays, the building will open from 10am-5.30pm as a shared workspace across the front of house areas, with a buffet lunch served from 1pm costing just £5.00 for Writers’ Card Members. Lunch will also be an opportunity to meet fellow-writers across our artistic community, and to chat with Royal Court staff.

Capacity is limited and bookings can only be made individually, with dates and booking periods advertised through the Writers’ Card Newsletter. There will also be options to include allergy and dietary information when booking.
name: Writers' Card: Writers' Canteen

description:
Struggling to focus on your own? Keep putting off starting a draft, finishing a rewrite or getting an idea out of your head and onto the page? We know the feeling…

Once a month, the Royal Court will host a Zoom focus session for writers, where we’ll hold each other to account for getting some proper work done. Free and open for all Writers’ Card Members to attend, these two-hour sessions will be a place to support dedicated, quiet creative work for anyone who needs the extra push.

Each Zoom session will be hosted by a member of the Royal Court’s artistic team. At the start we will take five minutes to go around, introduce ourselves, and state our ambitions and intentions for the two-hour period.

All participants will be asked to turn their microphones off for the duration of the meeting, but invited to keep video turned on for accountability as they prefer.  And, of course, you can join or depart the session as you need.

Participants are invited to ask questions of one another using the Zoom chat feature (e.g., inviting creative input, brainstorming, etc.), but with no obligation for anyone to join the chat.

At the end, we’ll do ten minutes when anyone who wants to can turn their microphone back on and share what progress they’ve made, and any commitment they want to make for their own next steps.
name: Writers' Card: Zoom Focus Sessions
